findings.title: [P1] Restore message-listener removal in `unmount`
findings.body: Triggered by any `mount(socket)` → `unmount()` cycle followed by further socket activity. The new `mount()` registers an anonymous closure (`socket.on("message", message => this.render(message))`) whose reference is never kept, and the new `unmount()` only does `this.socket = undefined` — the previous `this.socket?.off("message", this.onMessage)` deregistration is gone. Since `off()` requires the exact handler reference, the listener can no longer be detached at all. Consequences: an unmounted view keeps rendering on every subsequent `"message"` event; repeated mount/unmount cycles accumulate one closure per mount and amplify each message into multiple `render` calls; and any socket that outlives the view retains the view and its closure, preventing garbage collection. Restore the stored-handler pattern (or equivalent) so `unmount()` can actually detach the listener.

findings.title: [P3] Add listener-lifecycle regression coverage with the fix
findings.body: The repository contains no tests (and no test infrastructure) for `SocketView`, and this PR changes exactly the behavior most in need of protection — listener registration/detachment. When fixing the P1 above, add a regression test that emits a `"message"` event after `unmount()` and asserts rendering no longer occurs. Rated P3 rather than higher because the absence of any test setup is a pre-existing repo-wide condition, not something this PR introduced.

findings.title: [nit] Confirm the intended contract for an unreferenced `SocketView`
findings.body: A source-wide search finds no callers of `SocketView` outside `src/socket-view.ts` itself, so no in-repo usage validates whether weakening `unmount()` was intentional. Worth confirming the intended lifecycle contract before merge, since the PR description claims existing contracts are preserved.
